title: Market Day
sub: A small game about why people buy. Mind a stall at a hill market, set the prices, choose the sign, and watch the villagers decide. Then come back for Festival day and a Winter market.
description: Market Day: a small browser game by Riya Dutta. Three market days, twelve nudges and eleven villagers. Set the prices, pick the sign, and learn why each one buys or walks away.
facts: A game in the browser, nothing to download
Price tags and a chalkboard sign; a free-taste tray and prices ending in 9 at the festival; a chai and walnut bundle in winter
A first market day, Festival day and a Winter market, where happy customers come back
The idea, the villagers, the drawing and the rules
One HTML file: every villager drawn in SVG, every sound and voice made in the browser

hero.alt: Riya waving beside her market stall of honey jars, apples, a woollen cap and a shawl, with a chalkboard that says Fresh this morning

sections.title: Price it, sign it, open up.
sections.note: Tap Set prices to change the price tags, then tap the chalkboard to choose what it says. Open the stall, and change things once at lunch. At dusk, the ledger shows who bought, why, and how much more they would have paid. Finish a day to unlock the next.

items.t: Most of marketing is a nudge, not a price cut. Here you can watch twelve of them at work on eleven shoppers, one at a time.
Every villager has a limit, and the right nudge stretches it. The ledger shows each reason and each limit, so the next day you can price a little smarter.

tiles.d: Pip the goat pays more for the medium honey when the big jar costs twice as much: the decoy. Kiko the yak pays more for a cap when the shawl beside it is pricey: the anchor.
Juno the monal pays up to ₹150 for apples if stock looks short. Nell the pika pays ₹120, but only once a crowd has bought. Price the apples for one, and you may lose the other.
Wren the red panda wants to know where it was made. Tell her it is local, and keep the small jar at ₹200 or less.

Lumi the marmot buys after a free taste. Bo the snow leopard cub hates to miss the last day of the season. Gus the black bear loves a price ending in 9, and eats every free taste. Pip and Wren come back loyal if you won them the day before.

Milo the ibex loves a bundle that costs less than its parts. Dot the snow partridge pays more when ₹10 goes to the school. Tess the Tibetan fox buys a ₹1,800 shawl once it is “under ₹5 a day”. Kiko and Bo come back, and Lumi and Gus are hibernating.

paras: The rest of this site is work for clients. The Lab is for things I make because I want them to exist. This one turns the ideas I use every day into three days at a hill market, from a sunny morning to a festival to the first snow. A perfect day is possible on each, but it takes the right prices, and the right nudge at the right time.
